title: One added stimulus signal cannot match saved mouse visual spectra if VISp geometry is kept up to overall gain
abstract: We tested a retained VISp stimulus kernel plus added positive stimulus signals. Interlacing gives a necessary signal count. A linear program gives the smallest normalized target-spectrum change that permits one added signal. For the first 30 saved mean cvPCA values, VISam needs at least 3 added signals in Neuropixels and 8 in two-photon covariance surrogates. A one-signal model needs target L1 changes of 0.03590 and 0.12355. Different VISp draws also fail the strict test, so these are not animal-level rejections. We also derive the exact kernel of Gaussian squared-feature pooling with unequal image energy. It has a shared rank-one term that can dominate as pooling width grows. Projection away from the input-energy direction removes this term and makes the residual independent of width. This model can leave an equal-energy activation class. The one-signal test does not reject the full pooling model, which can also change the residual geometry. No new animals or raw recordings enter this study.

display.caption: Necessary signal rank, one-signal error margin, and a synthetic energy-pooling control. These are surrogate tests, not animal confidence intervals.
